format.inherits: Every rule of cp4_golden parts 1 and 2 'format' applies (including benchmark_expected, comparability, v_beta, decomposition_view, bites).
format.valuation_mode: Assertion level. Absent = historical mode with 'as_of'. 'CURRENT' with 'instant' t (UTC): the engine resolves the as-of date D_c(t) by performance Ruling 1.7 (1.12); each item asserts it as 'as_of_resolved'. Risk Ruling 5.8 (1.2) governs the benchmark, its fixing and the risk-free quote at t.
format.scope: Item level. Absent = the portfolio. {kind: ACCOUNT, account_id}: the account scope of risk Ruling 0.1 (internal transfers are flows of the account); benchmark-dependent items use the portfolio's selection.
format.default_view: Kind 'default_view' (risk Ruling 7.7 (1.2), PD-0040): a SERVICE-LEVEL composition, not a metric. Input: metric, frequency, default_request. Output: 'fallback' (true when the default request was refused for history and MAX_AVAILABLE is shown), 'refused' (the default request's result summary when it fell back, else null), 'shown' (the summary of what the view shows: request, requested_base, effective_window, state, reason, value, exact, exact_square, sign, details_include). The engine exposes the composition as one function; the two underlying results are ordinary metric results and reproduce on their own.
format.benchmark_selections: (1.2-part3) As part 2, plus per record: record_type SELECT | CLEAR | REVERSAL (absent = SELECT when benchmark_id is set, else CLEAR); reverses_selection_id (REVERSAL); corrects_selection_id (the replacement of a correction pair); atomic_with_seq (the two records of a correction pair are appended in ONE transaction, migration 0015).
format.selection_resolution: (1.2-part3) Item kind. Asserts the resolution of the pinned selection-log version alone: selection {state NONE | CLEARED | IN_FORCE | REFUSED, selection_id, seq, benchmark_id} of the record in force (risk Ruling 5.6 (1.4)). REFUSED: the version cuts a correction pair, so it cannot be pinned (the engine's refusal, whatever its error type).
format.synthetic: Every result computed for this fixture is synthetic (market-data Ruling 4.8).

market_data.how_to_load: As cp4_golden parts 1 and 2: the loader expands these compact definitions into synthetic files in the real layouts, registers them with upstream 'synthetic' (the two sources of SYN4_BM_US_TR2 with the declared upstreams synthetic_a and synthetic_b, the two sides of risk Ruling 5.7 (1.2)), and ingests them into one release M. (1.1) Each series is delivered in the three files (vintages) of 'retrieval', by row date, with the declared retrieval times; the 1.0 declaration 'retrieval_time_all_files' (2022-11-30T00:00:00Z) is withdrawn: a file cannot hold closes after its retrieval time (market-data Ruling 3.1, after-retrieval test), so every series would have been contradicted.

retrieval.rule: A file's retrieval_time is at or after the availability instant (scheduled close; for FX and risk-free rates, publication) of every row it holds (market-data Ruling 3.1). At each Current-mode instant of this fixture, M_t (performance Ruling 1.7: the files retrieved at or before t) holds exactly the rows whose availability instant is at or before t. Historical-mode assertions read all of M. cp4_part3_calculator.py --retrieval verifies both properties.
retrieval.files: One file per (series, vintage); the ECB file per vintage holds every currency; a series on calendar c takes the V2 time of c. A vintage with no row for a series is not delivered for it.
retrieval.segments: (1.3-part3; market-data Ruling 0.1 (1.12)) Each vintage's rows range is its file's declared COVERAGE interval: V1 [the series' first date, 2026-01-08], V2 [2026-01-09, 2026-01-09], V3 [2026-01-10, the series' last date]. The three files of a series are SEGMENTS of ONE series: disjoint coverage, one identity (source, subject, adjustment status, anchor, declared fields, synthetic flag), and every series here is vintage-stable (RAW prices, ECB fixings, published benchmark levels, risk-free quotes). The vintage is the file's retrieval_time; no vintage label is written into adjustment_anchor or any other identity field (anchor null). The release build joins the segments; the read path sees one series.

market_data.benchmarks_rule: As part 2, plus: (a) several entries with one benchmark_id are the SOURCES of that benchmark, ordered by source_priority (1 = primary); 'level_overrides' replaces the level of single calculation days of that source only (Ruling 5.7 (1.2)). (1.9-part3) A benchmark with several sources declares 'official_decimals' (the index's published precision) and each source 'precision_decimals' (Ruling 5.7 (1.9)); a level's text shows at most its source's declared decimals. (b) construction ETF_PROXY: no levels are supplied; the engine builds the gross total-return index from the listing's RAW closes and its cash dividends in corporate_actions (Ruling 5.5 (1.2)).
market_data.corporate_actions_rule: As cp3_golden: synthetic FEED and FILING records, both synthetic, are the two sides of market-data Ruling 4.5 (Ruling 4.8 item 4(a)). For a CASH_DIVIDEND each record carries its own amount; equal amounts on both sides = CORROBORATED, one side only = SINGLE_SOURCE, different amounts = DISAGREEMENT. (1.7-part3) For an ETF proxy, statements of separate entries are matched across sides by risk Ruling 5.5 (1.7): equal statements pair; statements sharing the record date, ex-date or pay date are one dividend; unpaired statements of the two sides whose ex-dates are at most 20 sessions apart are one possibly mis-dated dividend (DISAGREEMENT); the rest are SINGLE_SOURCE. (1.8-part3) A CASH_DIVIDEND entry's 'currency' is the declared currency; a record may add 'paid_currency' and 'paid_amount', the issuer's stated payment (market-data Ruling 7.1). A proxy converts by risk Ruling 5.5 (1.8).

portfolios.name: R1 (USD; SYN21) against a FLAT total-return index

assertions.purpose: A benchmark that never moves (S_bb = 0): beta, R-squared and alpha are undefined (ZERO_BENCHMARK_VARIANCE); TE equals the portfolio's volatility; IR is the portfolio's mean return over its volatility; the window facts are omitted (against a flat index they cannot discriminate).

portfolios.name: R2 (USD; SYN42, whose 2025-06-13 print is missing) against the US index

assertions.purpose: A LAGGED grid date inside a statistic's window: on Friday 2025-06-13 the holding is valued at Thursday's close (1 session missed, AVAILABLE + STALE_DATA) while the benchmark is current. 3Y: AVAILABLE + STALE_DATA, comparability LIMITED, one lagged point (1 against 0).

(1.1) Which causes give the reason (risk Ruling 7.3 (1.3), performance Ruling 1.5 (1.1)): over 1Y the result is LIMITED by its count (a cause with no code), and the 06-13 period is AVAILABLE + STALE_DATA (a lower-level cause with a code). The reason is none; STALE_PERIODS stays in the details. Reading the reason from every level would give STALE_DATA (M-C24).

portfolios.name: R3 (USD; SYN21) against a CN index in CNY whose translation is stale on 2025-03-14

assertions.purpose: Stale FX on the benchmark leg only: CNY quotes missing 2025-03-13/14, so at 03-14 the benchmark's translation is 2 fixings stale (LIMITED + STALE_DATA) and its lag is 2 against the portfolio's 0 (LAGGED). The portfolio holds no foreign currency. SEAM: {NYSE} against {ECB, SSE}. The window facts read 2025-01-10 and 2026-01-02 only, so they are not stale.

portfolios.name: R4 (USD; SYN21) against a US index published by two sources

assertions.purpose: Two sources (Ruling 5.7): they disagree on 2025-08-08 only (990.00 against 991.00), so that day's level is INSUFFICIENT_DATA + SOURCE_CONFLICT and every statistic whose window contains it is too. The window facts read 2025-01-10 and 2026-01-02, where the sources agree: AVAILABLE.
A window fact ending on the disagreement: INSUFFICIENT_DATA + SOURCE_CONFLICT.
The primary source has no level on Friday 2025-09-12; the second source has it, so the datum exists (SINGLE_SOURCE), is current, and is used.

(1.9-part3; risk Ruling 5.7 (1.9), review finding CP4F-13) SYN4_BM_US_TR5: the index publishes 2 decimals (official_decimals 2); source a renders them (precision 2: bound 0), source b rounds to 1 decimal (precision 1, declared: bound 0.05) and its texts happen to show none (990). On 2025-08-08 a says 990.30, b says 990: |0.30| > 0 + 0.05, a DISAGREEMENT. Inferring b's precision from its texts (0 decimals: bound 0.5, M-C45) would call them in agreement and use 990.30.

(1.9-part3; risk Ruling 5.7 (1.9)) SYN4_BM_US_TR4 is served by two sources with no declared precision: it cannot be reconciled, so it is not a usable series: MISSING_BENCHMARK, BENCHMARK_SERIES_UNAVAILABLE. Reconciling it anyway (M-C44) gives a number.

portfolios.name: R5 (USD; SYN21) against two ETF proxies

assertions.purpose: ETF proxy (Ruling 5.5 as of 1.2): total return built from SYN31's RAW closes and its dividends: 0.50 on 2025-03-03 (feed and filing agree: CORROBORATED) and 0.40 on 2025-09-02 (feed only: SINGLE_SOURCE, used).

The second proxy's 2025-06-02 dividend is 0.30 in the feed and 0.35 in the filing (DISAGREEMENT): the proxy is INSUFFICIENT_DATA + SOURCE_CONFLICT from that ex-date on, until a resolution record exists.
The same proxy over a window that ends before the disputed ex-date: AVAILABLE.

(1.6-part3; risk Ruling 5.5 (1.6)) The disputed SYN32 dividend (ex 2025-06-02) BREAKS the proxy chain at its ex-date: a window after it (g_0 = 2025-06-06) needs no ratio that spans the break, so it is AVAILABLE. Benchmark 50/50.50 - 1 = -1/101 (06-06 phase 2 to 01-02 phase 0, no dividend after the break); portfolio 100/101 - 1 = -1/101; active 0.

(1.6-part3; risk Ruling 5.5 (1.6)) SYN33's two price sources disagree on Wednesday 2025-08-06, an interior non-grid day: that print is withheld, the chain links 08-05 to 08-07 around it (no price of 08-06 is needed), and no grid date uses it. So the 1Y beta and the window facts are what they would be without the dispute. Withholding every later print (M-C33, the engineer's current proxy) refuses them.

(1.6-part3) The second SYN33 dispute falls on Friday 2026-01-09, g_n itself: the level g_n needs is withheld, so the window facts are INSUFFICIENT_DATA + SOURCE_CONFLICT (BENCHMARK_SOURCE_CONFLICT). Treating the disputed print as a missing one (M-C34) would use Thursday's level, 1 print stale, and report a number.

(1.7-part3; risk Ruling 5.5 (1.7)) SYN34: the feed states a 0.50 dividend ex 2025-03-03 (pay 03-10), the filing a 0.50 dividend ex 2025-03-05 (pay 03-12). They share no date, and their ex-dates are 2 sessions apart: possibly ONE dividend stated with different dates, so a DISAGREEMENT, and the chain breaks at both ex-dates. A window spanning them is INSUFFICIENT_DATA + SOURCE_CONFLICT. Applying both as two single-source dividends (M-C36, the engineer's decision 1) double-counts 0.50 and gives a number.

(1.7-part3) After the break (g_0 = 2025-06-06): the feed's 0.40 ex 2025-09-02 and the filing's 0.40 ex 2025-12-01 share no date and are far more than 20 sessions apart: two dividends, each SINGLE_SOURCE, both applied. Benchmark (50/50.50)(50.90/50.50)(49.90/49.50) - 1 = 6065/1009899; portfolio -1/101; active -16064/1009899.

Metamorphic: R8's account-scope A1 statistics, and R12's (split recorded), equal part 2's Q1 exactly (beta 505685421350637/350647849329134). R1's tracking error equals the portfolio's volatility, and its IR equals the portfolio's mean return over its volatility (the benchmark contributes nothing).

No look-ahead in Current mode: R7-C1 and R7-H1 differ, and R7-C1's benchmark level date (2026-01-08) and fixing date (2026-01-08) are both before the instant's unavailable 2026-01-09 close and publication.

RD-1 and RS-1 (parts 1 and 2) hold on every part-3 item with a value; account-scope identities: the account-level money gains sum to the portfolio's (performance Ruling 4.5), the account-level returns do not.
Determinism: byte-identical canonical results across runs and PYTHONHASHSEED values.

(1.2-part3) Selection-log appends refused (risk Ruling 5.6 (1.4)): a REVERSAL of a REVERSAL; a second REVERSAL of one record; a REVERSAL or replacement naming another portfolio's record; a replacement whose REVERSAL is not in the same append. A result pinned at R13 version 2 names seq 2 (the CN index) and reproduces so for ever; at version 3 the selection in force is seq 1, so the version-2 result is superseded, and the cause the evidence states is the reversal (seq 3) of the record it used.

release_cases.rule: (1.3-part3; 1.4-part3 adds RB-6 to RB-9 and the two outcomes of market-data Ruling 0.1 (1.13)) The outcome of building M from each case's file set, all files being of ONE series key unless a case says otherwise. Checked in order: identity (adjustment_status, anchor, synthetic flag, and every other declared field) -> REFUSED_IDENTITY; a series in several files that is not vintage-stable -> REFUSED_NOT_SEGMENTABLE; (1.13) a file of a series in several files whose coverage cannot be stated -> REFUSED_COVERAGE_UNDETERMINED; (1.13) a file of a series in several files holding a row outside its declared coverage -> REFUSED_ROW_OUTSIDE_COVERAGE; any two files whose COVERAGE intervals share a date -> REFUSED_OVERLAP, with the union of the shared intervals; otherwise ADMITTED as one series of 'segments' files. 'rows': 'series' = the fixture's SYN42 rows inside the coverage (no row on 2025-06-13), or inside 'rows_range' when the coverage is null; a map = exactly those rows; 'extra_rows' = rows the file ALSO holds. These cases are release-build outcomes, not metric items; the engine's refusal is its TwoVintages error (or equivalent), whatever its type name. They bite the points-only reading.

mutation_catalog.M-R1: disjoint POINTS (rows held) instead of disjoint coverage
mutation_catalog.M-R2: a vendor-adjusted series may be segmented
mutation_catalog.M-R3: overlapping files are admitted when their rows agree on every date of the overlap
mutation_catalog.M-R4: a series in more than one file is always refused (Ruling 0.1 as written in 1.11)
mutation_catalog.M-R5: a row outside the declared coverage WIDENS the coverage to the hull of the interval and the rows
mutation_catalog.M-R6: a row outside the declared coverage is ignored (the coverage is the declared interval, rows are not checked against it)
mutation_catalog.M-R7: a segment whose coverage cannot be stated is given the hull of its rows

cases.purpose: The fixture's own vintages of SYN42: three disjoint coverage segments of one RAW series.

A backfill: file V1b, retrieved with V1, holds a 101.00 print for 2025-06-13, the date V1 covers WITHOUT a row (no print). The points are disjoint, the coverage is not: 'no print' became 'a print', a revision of 2025-06-13. Admitting it would also silently change R2 (its 06-13 staleness and lag).
A re-download of V3's dates (V3r, retrieved a day later) with identical rows: still two vintages of 2026-01-10..2026-03-31, refused even though every value agrees.

A vendor-adjusted series (DIVIDEND_ADJUSTED, SUBTRACTIVE, anchor LATEST) in two disjoint segments: refused, because each retrieval re-bases the whole history (Ruling 2.3) and the join would be a false jump.
Control: V2 declared real (synthetic false) among synthetic segments: one identity is required (market-data Ruling 4.8: a synthetic and a real series never meet).

(1.4-part3; review finding CP4M-10) V2 declares coverage 2026-01-09 only but also holds a 101.00 row for 2025-06-13, a date V1 covers with no row. The row outside V2's declared coverage refuses the build (market-data Ruling 0.1 (1.13) item 1(c)). Ignoring it (M-R6) re-creates RB-2 with two readings of 06-13; widening V2's coverage to the hull (M-R5) refuses for a different, fabricated overlap 2025-06-13..2026-01-08.

(1.4-part3) V3 declares coverage from 2026-01-10 but also holds the 2026-01-09 row (103.00, the same value V2 holds): a row before its declared start, a second reading of 01-09. Refused (item 1(c)), whatever the values.

(1.4-part3) V2 states no coverage (no requested range, not a full-history file): in a series of several files its coverage cannot be stated, so disjointness cannot be shown. REFUSED_COVERAGE_UNDETERMINED (item 1(b)). Inferring it from the rows (M-R7) would let the content define its own claim.

(1.4-part3) Why not the hull: no V2, so 2026-01-09 lies in a hole no file covers, and V3 (declared from 2026-01-10) holds a 2026-01-09 row anyway. The hull (M-R5) would ADMIT it, so a row the file was not asked for, outside the file's own statement of what it holds, would value 01-09. Refused (item 1(c)).
